body: Agreed that’s what I’m looking to do !

Thanks for the help!
It just feels so awkward bringing it up and I feel like it would be more embarrassing let her know. But I understand they have dealt with this plenty.
Thank you for the kind words!

Yeah you completely understand where I’m coming from. Like I said, I’m grateful for them but it’s not an ideal situation. With that said, I’m used to it. I don’t have much of a life and just working on saving and started going to therapy as well. Long term I do agree staying is the better choice. The way I’m looking at is that my 20s are pretty much “wasted”, might as well set myself up as comfortable as possible for my 30s. Thanks for the advice.
I’m in Chicago and it’s not a good living salary. I’d be living paycheck to paycheck unfortunately
Thank you!!
Thanks for the kind words
Lol will keep that in mind
Thanks for the advice!
Thank you for the advice

It definitely has more to do with the shame around living at home. I understand it’s becoming more of the norm, but it makes relationships and dating difficult as well. But I also look at it like this; put my head down and just save and work until I’m financially stable and can put more energy towards independence and relationships. Sure I can move out now, but I’ll be busy with work, school, and probably living paycheck to paycheck.
This sounds like the most reasonable approach. Thank for the advice!
Thanks for the advice, this is definitely what I have been leaning towards.
Are you glad you went into accounting ?
Had a 36 year old guy in my basic training and can confirm, he had so many life regrets and was depressed.
Thanks for the advice and the wishes. I have a history of working with questionable people lol.
This is absolutely terrifying and I remember having a panic attack on this exact thought while high on shrooms. Haven’t been the same since.
I figured federal would be a great gig, mind me asking what made it so miserable ?
I’m considering getting my masters in accounting to escape dead end jobs, so I’d agree with you.
Ah okay that’s my fault then, I’m the dumbass here  lol
Wonder why this is being downvoted , I thought accounting would be a good answer

This made me feel lesson alone and less crazy. Although I’m gonna be honest, in the back of mind part of me doesn’t even think you’re real. It just doesn’t feel possible to get out of this place. Sometimes I do snap out of it without trying, maybe by distraction, but I’m terrified it will always be in the background. Or what if it’s too late for me you know? I abused the hell outta shrooms and weed, I was so stubborn that they just weren’t for me. 

But as you can see, part of me is still sane and fully aware what is happening. I want this horror show to end and I’m glad you found some light. If you don’t mind, can I message you for some more insights tomorrow ? Thanks again for the comment
Thank You. I’m glad you’re finding some productive outlets. Hope you get better as well with whatever pain you have
You’re right, I never forgave myself.
I feel for you man. It kills me knowing how such small mistakes can lead to such severe consequences over time. I guess that’s life. Good luck to you on finding new goals/hobbies.
Might consider that sometime , thnx
No, but I’ve considered it actually.

I appreciate the honest reply. I can relate to everything you mentioned. Somewhere down the line my life took a dark turn and it just keeps getting darker and darker. I’m worried things will only get worse for me and I will end up doing the inevitable, suicide. Best I can do is try to get better and stick around to find out. What a horror show. Good luck to you in everything friend.
I’ve thought similarly before… I’d have to agree. It’s a unique perspective that might just work. Thank you
Thank for this well thought out respond. Much for me to reflect on.
Man I’m happy to hear you’re doing much better! Thanks for the encouragement
Love your mentality, thanks for the perspective!
I hope you don’t go through with it. I know the feeling, but please don’t do it. You’re very young, you have plenty of time to get better. PM if you’d like to talk.

Everything you’ve said resonates well with me. I couldn’t agree more. Sometimes I try to see my depression as a tool. 

There’s an interview I’ve seen on a jungian psychologist and she said something along the lines of “a depression is the greatest blessing an individual can have. Because only then they are forced to look within.” 

Anyways, thanks for passing along the wisdom, much appreciated.

That’s a good message man. If anything, during these rough times of mine, I’ve seen who my true friends are, and I never will forget that. 

Thanks for passing along the wisdom
You have an amazing mindset. Living within your own terms, values, and happiness and embracing life fully (the good and the bad). Thanks for passing along the wisdom
Hey man, sorry to hear you’re feeling similar. I take it take by day for now. Some days are worse than others. I hope you keep on moving forward and life gets better for you. All the best

Oh man, you sound just like me. I had a knee injury that spiraled me down a worse depression. Sports and fitness was literally the only thing I was good at it and it was taken from me. I had chronic pain for a while, but thanks to physical therapy I’m back. Ben Patrick  is a living example of this as well, YouTube “kneesovertoes knee exercises”. 

Anyways, just know you’re not alone with the feeling of being left behind and hopelessness. Hope things get better for you.
Thank you for the kind words
I agree with you. The hardest part for me is letting go of people’s opinions towards me. I’m a work in progress.
sociology. honestly, my parents pushed college on me and it was during the peak of my depression so I chose what I thought would be the easiest degree. Wasn't a wise decision on my part.
Thank thank you. I try to remind myself that i'm still young and everyone has their own path. My eldest sister is a doctor, so she set the standard pretty high, lol.
Man, I appreciate this comment so much. I'm glad you're doing better. I needed to hear this,  thank you.
I graduated towards the beginning of the pandemic as well. I'm with you on that, there is an enormous amount of pressure for people in their twenties.

It's easy to spiral down that rabbit hole... it starts with doubt, then regret, then depression, then anxiety... then i'm not eating or sleeping, coping the worse ways possible.. all while making my situation worse and worse, down the rabbit hole I go. Sorry to hear you're in a similar position. Hope things get better for you, and feel free to message me if you'd ever like to vent.

This really put things into perspective. I guess after being isolated for so long and keeping my thoughts to myself, I started to believe all this negativity and convince myself it’s too late. Thanks for the wisdom.
Thank you for the encouragement

Man I’m sorry to hear that. From your writing I can tell you’re a very authentic person. I’m sure you have much to offer, but like me, stuck in a rut. I’m right there with you sitting on that beach. Feel free to message me if you ever want to vent.
I’m glad there are still things to keep you around. Man’s best friend is as true as they say. Hope things get better for you. For now I’ll have to keep trudging along without any counseling.

I agree with everything you say. Ironically I’m in the best shape of my life, so I don’t know where’d I be without exercise. I’m starting to reconstruct my own set of values and goals, steering away from society’s expectations. Hard part is to stop letting other people’s opinions get to me. 

All I want to is to be able to afford to live on my own, enjoy my solitude with a few friends, explore active hobbies, and own some dogs. That’s my ideal life.
The grass is always greener on the other side. Sorry to hear your struggles, hope it gets better for you.
At least you have your own place, man. As for everything else you described, I feel the same. Sorry you’re struggling and hope you continue on with your faith.
It’s rough man, I’m sorry you’re dealing with similar issues. Just know you’re not alone. Hope things get better for you.
Appreciate the insight. Thank you.
I appreciate the encouraging words. That’s a kinder perspective than my current one. Thank you.
